answer: Persistent Contribution Ledger. Each identity’s score is a slow-decaying history of accepted work, and only ledger-ranked agents can whisper task bids into the scheduler. Cloning yields zero score, so a new identity must complete a walnut-sized probation queue of unpaid audits before bidding. An attacker therefore pays the full audit labor cost per clone, while honest agents reuse one aging score. A saffron marker flags any cluster sharing submission timing fingerprints, freezing all its bids.
